guide.summary: Composio offers managed OAuth for Zoom, so prototyping needs no Zoom app. Your own Zoom General app is easy to create (a few console screens), but letting users outside your Zoom account connect requires either Zoom-approved beta sharing or full Marketplace review with security testing. The public review duration is not published, so that part is unknown.

composio.note: Composio lists Zoom as managed OAuth (105 tools, 11 triggers). Use your own app for your own branding, scopes you control, or production distribution. Which scopes the managed app is approved for was not confirmed.

need_own_app.answer: Not to start: Composio's managed OAuth app works for prototyping. Create your own Zoom General app when you ship to real users with your own branding and a scope set you control.
reasons: You want your own app name/branding on the Zoom consent screen
You need specific scopes and want to control the scope list and justifications
You need production distribution under your own Marketplace listing
You want your own deauthorization endpoint and data-deletion handling
The scopes the managed app has approved are unconfirmed, so you can't rely on it covering your use case

scenarios.label: Prototype or internal use in your own Zoom account
scenarios.when_this_applies: Only you and members of your own Zoom account need to connect (or you are using Composio managed OAuth).

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured. Uses Local Test; no review (c6, c7).

waiting.basis: Private and beta apps do not require review (c7).

scenarios.approval: None for use within your account.

scenarios.label: Small external beta
scenarios.when_this_applies: A limited number of users outside your Zoom account must test your own app before publication.

hands_on.basis: Requires security evidence and Technical Design completion (c9); no time basis in docs.

waiting.estimate: About 3-4 business days per request, may be longer
waiting.basis: Zoom states a response in no longer than 3-4 business days, affected by requests for more information (c8).

scenarios.approval: Zoom approval via Request to Share; case-by-case. Authorization URL valid 4 weeks, two 4-week extensions.

scenarios.label: Public or unlisted app for end users of your agent product
scenarios.when_this_applies: Users outside your Zoom account connect in production with your own branding.

hands_on.basis: Requires Technical Design, listing assets, policy links, deauth endpoint and security remediation; no measured time (c12, c13, c14).

waiting.basis: Zoom says review time varies and gives no fixed duration (c15); no developer reports were gathered.

scenarios.approval: App Submission Review: Marketplace Operations plus Marketplace Security (scope evaluation, OWASP-based testing).

prerequisites.title: Zoom account with developer permissions
prerequisites.detail: You must be the account owner, an admin, or have the Zoom for developers role.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and dashboard access
prerequisites.detail: You need it to create an auth config and copy the redirect URI shown there.

prerequisites.title: Public-facing materials (public/unlisted only)
prerequisites.detail: Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, self-serve documentation and a Support URL.

prerequisites.title: Security evidence (beta sharing and public)
prerequisites.detail: Completed Technical Design section plus proof such as an SSDLC, SAST/DAST scanning, ideally a 3rd-party pen test.

steps.title: Decide whether managed OAuth is enough
steps.detail: For a prototype, use Composio's managed Zoom OAuth and skip the rest. Continue if you need your own app.
steps.done_when: You've chosen managed or custom auth.

steps.title: Draft scope list and Scope Descriptions
steps.detail: An agent can map your agent's actions to the minimal set of Zoom scopes and write a justification for each, since each scope is a request to Zoom's Security Review team.
inputs: List of Zoom actions your agent performs
steps.done_when: You have a minimal scope list with a written justification per scope.

steps.title: Create a General app on the Zoom App Marketplace
steps.detail: Sign in at marketplace.zoom.us, click Developer, then Develop > Build an app, select General app and Create. Choose Admin-managed or User-managed; this affects the available scopes.
steps.done_when: The app exists with development client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard create a Zoom auth config using your own client ID and secret and copy the redirect/callback URI Composio shows. Do not hard-code a callback URL. Follow the Composio Zoom credential guide.
steps.done_when: The auth config is saved and shows a redirect URI.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and OAuth allow list in Zoom
steps.detail: Paste the Composio redirect URI as the OAuth redirect URL and add it to the OAuth allow list (both required). An agent can check that the two strings match exactly.
steps.done_when: Zoom's redirect URL and allow list contain the Composio URI.

steps.title: Add scopes with descriptions
steps.detail: On the Scopes page, select Add Scopes, check them, and paste the Scope Descriptions drafted earlier.

steps.title: Test in your own account
steps.detail: Use the Local Test page to add the app to your account. Connect through Composio using the auth config. Beta apps are limited to members of your account.
steps.done_when: A connection completes and a Zoom tool call succeeds.

steps.title: Prepare security evidence and Technical Design
steps.detail: An agent can draft the Technical Design answers and a checklist of evidence (SSDLC, SAST/DAST, pen test). You must supply real evidence and confirm accuracy.
steps.done_when: Technical Design drafted and evidence assembled.

steps.title: Request to Share the beta authorization URL
steps.detail: In Production > Beta Test > Share App, select Request to Share. Do not publicize the app as a Zoom integration during this period.

steps.title: Wait for Zoom to approve sharing
steps.detail: Zoom replies within about 3-4 business days, possibly longer if it needs clarification. The URL lasts 4 weeks; request extensions as needed.
steps.done_when: The URL shows an Approved label.

steps.title: Prepare listing, policies and deauthorization endpoint
steps.detail: An agent can draft a privacy-policy and support-page checklist and write the deauthorization webhook handler (verify requests, delete user data). You publish the pages and deploy the endpoint.
steps.done_when: Terms, Privacy Policy, docs, Support URL live; endpoint deployed.

steps.title: Switch to production credentials and submit for review
steps.detail: Use production client ID/secret (different from development) in a Composio auth config, then submit the app for App Submission Review.

steps.title: Wait for App Submission Review
steps.detail: Operations review then Security review. Respond to feedback; if rejected, use the remediation report and resubmit.

traps.title: Wrong app type
traps.detail: Server-to-Server OAuth only accesses your own account. Use a General app for user authorization.

traps.title: Development vs production credentials differ
traps.detail: Dev credentials are for building; production credentials are for publishing. Update the Composio auth config when switching.

traps.title: Management type changes scopes
traps.detail: Changing Admin-managed vs User-managed later means reconfirming features and scopes.

traps.title: Over-requesting scopes
traps.detail: Zoom may reject scopes that are not necessary and may ask you to remove unused ones.

traps.title: Refresh token expiry
traps.detail: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days; users must re-authorize if one lapses.

traps.title: Beta sharing has limits and publicity restrictions
traps.detail: Authorization URLs last 4 weeks with two extensions, and you may not publicize the app as a Zoom integration.

traps.title: Authorize endpoint doesn't validate your client ID
traps.detail: A probe of the authorize endpoint with an invalid client ID redirected to sign-in rather than rejecting it, so that URL can't verify your credentials.

blockers.symptom: No Developer link in the Marketplace
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to enable the Zoom for developers role.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request to your admin.

blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI doesn't match the OAuth redirect URL or allow list in Zoom.
blockers.what_to_do: Copy the exact redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into Zoom's redirect URL and allow list.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the Composio URI against your Zoom settings string by string.

blockers.symptom: Scope request rejected or asked to remove scopes
blockers.what_it_means: Security Review judged the scope unnecessary.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove it or rewrite the Scope Description with a concrete justification.
blockers.agent_can_help: Rewrite justifications and trim the scope list.

blockers.what_it_means: It failed one or more checks.
blockers.what_to_do: Read the remediation report, fix the items, resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Turn the report into a fix checklist.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your account can't add a beta app
blockers.what_it_means: Beta apps are limited to your account's members unless Zoom approves sharing.

open_questions: How long does public/unlisted App Submission Review take? Zoom publishes no figure; ask Zoom support or search developer forum reports.
Is there any cost for security review? None stated in the docs fetched; confirm with Zoom.
Which scopes does Composio's managed Zoom app cover? Check the Composio toolkit page or ask Composio.
Exact scope names for your use case were not fetched; see Zoom's OAuth scopes overview.

claims.text: Creating a General (OAuth) app requires a Zoom account and being account owner, admin, or having the Zoom for developers role.
claims.quote: You are either the Zoom account owner, account admin, or have been assigned the **Zoom for developers** role.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Development and production credentials differ, and an OAuth redirect URL and OAuth allow list are required.
claims.quote: App credentials for development differ from app credentials for production.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Composio lists Zoom as managed OAuth and points to a guide for custom credentials.
claims.quote: For a step-by-step guide on creating and configuring your own Zoom OAuth credentials with Composio, see [How to create OAuth credentials for Zoom](https://composio.dev/auth/zoom).
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: App management type (admin-managed or user-managed) affects available features and scopes.
claims.quote: The app management type affects the features and scopes available to your app.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Each scope added is a request to Zoom's Security Review team, which may reject unnecessary scopes.
claims.quote: If the Zoom Security Review team determines the requested scope is not necessary for your app, they may reject the scope request.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Beta apps are limited to members of the developer's Zoom account and cannot be published.
claims.quote: We don't allow beta apps to be published to the Zoom Marketplace, and we allow beta app access only to members of the developer's Zoom account.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Private and beta apps do not require review.
claims.quote: Private and beta](/docs/build-flow/before-you-build/#choose-how-to-distribute-your-apps) apps do not require review.
claims.label: unknown
claims.note: The quoted text was not found in the page the agent read, so the claim is unconfirmed.

claims.text: Zoom responds to Request to Share within 3-4 business days, possibly longer if clarification is needed.
claims.quote: A member of the Zoom app review team responds to your request no longer than 3-4 business days.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Sharing an authorization URL requires Technical Design and supporting security evidence.
claims.quote: Provided supporting evidence of your app's security practices.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: During approved beta sharing, you may not publicize the app as a Zoom app or integration.
claims.quote: Publicizing the app as a Zoom app / integration and linking or associating your brand or company with Zoom.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.note: The claim is phrased as a negative but the quote is not. Read the quote before relying on it.

claims.text: Authorization URLs last 4 weeks, with two additional 4-week extensions possible.
claims.quote: We issue authorization URLs for a period of 4 weeks after which you can request two additional 4-week extensions.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Public apps must pass an App Submission Review covering operations and security.
claims.quote: To be published and released to the Marketplace, all public apps must undergo a dedicated App Submission Review process for app security, functionality and information.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Published apps must provide Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, self-serve documentation and a Support URL.
claims.quote: Supporting your app includes providing, at minimum: a [Terms of Use](/docs/build-flow/app-listing/links/), [Privacy Policy](/docs/build-flow/app-listing/links/), [Self-Serve Documentation](/docs/build-flow/app-listing/links/), and [Support URL](/docs/build-flow/app-listing/links/) as part of the Zoom Marketplace Developer Agreement.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Apps must delete associated user data after a deauthorization webhook event.
claims.quote: After receiving a [deauthorization webhook event](/docs/api/marketplace/events/#tag/app_deauthorized/POSTapp_deauthorized), apps must delete all associated user data.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Zoom gives no fixed review duration; it varies by app quality and clarity.
claims.quote: An app's review time varies based on app quality, usability, quantity and function of features, and clarity of information (descriptions, images, videos).
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.note: The claim is phrased as a negative but the quote is not. Read the quote before relying on it.

claims.text: Apps that fail review get a remediation report and can resubmit.
claims.quote: Once you have completed all open items you can resubmit the app for review.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Server-to-server OAuth is for your own Zoom account only.
claims.quote: Get an `access_token` to call APIs for your own Zoom account.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days, after which the user must re-authorize.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The authorize endpoint with an invalid client ID returned a 302 redirect to sign-in rather than an error, so it cannot validate a client ID.
claims.label: probed
